source.title: Dissecting Adam: The Sign, Magnitude and Variance of Stochastic Gradients

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive, sign-based, and non-sign-based optimizers on trained networks and reports held-out performance, using a decomposition of Adam that differs from the optimizer comparisons in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports optimizer results on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and War and Peace, but its text does not describe those results as generalization-gap findings. Numerical curves appear only in figures; cited results from Wilson et al. are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD using training loss and test accuracy under individually tuned learning rates and fixed schedules. Its CIFAR-100 results test V4; decomposing Adam also examines which optimizer component accounts for the difference.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the main interpretation, but its causal wording should be softened: the authors interpret the CIFAR-100 comparison and theoretical extension as evidence implicating sign-based updates rather than adaptation alone. They conclude that sign-based updates dominate the tested optimizer differences, their usefulness depends on the problem, and variance adaptation can benefit non-sign-based updates.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Adam with momentum SGD, sign descent, and variance-adapted momentum SGD; it disentangles sign updates from variance adaptation rather than testing the full range of optimizers and tuning regimes in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimizer generalization effect differs between sign-based Adam/M - SSD and non-sign-based M - SVAG on CIFAR-100; the authors also state that sign usefulness is problem-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-adaptive momentum sign descent closely matches Adam's training and test behavior on CIFAR-100. The study also extends Wilson et al.'s constructed-example argument to sign descent, while explicitly declining to establish favorable generalization for M-SVAG theoretically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sign-based updates, rather than element-wise adaptation alone, can account for an optimizer's generalization disadvantage.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2018 proceedings; paper lists the 35th ICML, PMLR 80, 2018).
record.problems: The generalization comparison is described qualitatively, without numerical values or uncertainty in the prose; curves are in Figure 5. Results are reported for one CIFAR-100 architecture and one training schedule, and step sizes were individually tuned by maximal test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from the generalization discussion were omitted. Figure 5 reports curves for other tasks, but the text does not characterize their findings as optimizer-induced generalization-gap results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width changes beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language models. The language experiment here is character-level.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Controlled effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Other benchmark curves and supplementary optimizer comparisons are declared in rows_left_out. Their held-out results can bear on V4 even without an explicit generalization-gap discussion, but the supplied text does not preserve readable curve identities and values sufficient for additional directional verdicts. Figure 5 reports standard deviations over ten seeds; 'significantly worse' is the authors' wording, without a reported hypothesis test.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models; the experiment compares its own optimizer variants on CIFAR-100.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Sharpness and other measures tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: ADAM
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam and compared with momentum SGD and sign descent.

conditions.value: same data augmentation operations as for CIFAR-10

rows.value: Significantly worse test performance than M - SGD.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the paper.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is explicitly supported. Specify test accuracy, batch size 128, L2 regularization, and learning-rate reductions by 0.2 at 24k, 48k, and 64k steps. Learning rates were selected using maximum test accuracy; other optimizer parameters were fixed.

source_check.locator_found: Section 6.2, observation 4; Figure 5; Appendix A.1, CIFAR-100.

rows.subject: M - SSD
rows.operation_detail: Trained with momentum stochastic sign descent and compared with Adam and momentum SGD.

conditions.value: same data augmentation operations as for CIFAR-10

rows.value: Behaves almost identically to ADAM in both train and test; displays the same generalization-harming effects.
rows.note: The paper does not give numerical values in the prose.
rows.check: Momentum stochastic sign descent has no element-wise variance adaptation. Its similarity to Adam informs the proposed mechanism but does not itself measure an adaptive optimizer's performance relative to SGD as V4 specifies.

rows.subject: M - SVAG
rows.operation_detail: Trained with momentum SGD and variance adaptation, without the sign update.

conditions.value: same data augmentation operations as for CIFAR-10

rows.value: Improves upon M - SGD and does not display adverse effects on generalization.
rows.note: The result qualifies the optimizer comparison: this adaptive variant does not show Adam's stated generalization harm.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports that this adaptive method improves on momentum SGD, so its direction is opposite to the adaptive-method disadvantage, rather than a partial disadvantage. It qualifies extension to adaptive methods generally; it does not refute the claim that Adam often performs worse.
